title: Reached for ScheduleWakeup to wait on a Bash background task outside /loop
details:
**What happened:** Started a Bash command with `run_in_background: true`; it moved to background after timeout. Instead of just ending the turn and letting the harness's automatic background-completion notification resume me, I called ScheduleWakeup (a /loop-dynamic-mode tool) with a 90s delay to "wait" for it.
**What the user said:** User didn't comment; observed by the model.
**Repro:** Any non-/loop session: start `run_in_background` Bash, then call ScheduleWakeup instead of simply stopping the turn.
**Cause:** ScheduleWakeup's own tool description says it's for /loop dynamic mode and explicitly warns against scheduling short-interval wakeups to poll background work, but I misapplied it as a generic "wait for me" primitive in a plain (non-loop) session.
